newsitem.title: PERU: Police suspect rebels in Peru power firm bombing.
newsitem.headline: Police suspect rebels in Peru power firm bombing.

text.p: Suspected leftist rebels tossed a bomb at a Peruvian electric company, damaging the firm and other buildings but causing no injuries, police said early on Wednesday.
"We dont know who did it yet but we presume it was terrorist criminals," said an anti-terrorist police officer, who requested anonymity.
The officer, citing witnesses, said a bomb in a black bag exploded outside the front door of Edelnor's offices in Lima's poor northern district of Comas at about 11 p.m. Tuesday (0400 GMT Wednesday).
He said two men and a women were seen walking past the building and tossing a bag with the bomb at the front door of Edelnor.
Police and local radio said the blast destroyed the firm's front door, shattered windows in buildings in a radius of 600 feet (200 meters) and apparently damaged furniture and equipment inside.
Bomb squad officers were on the scene but could not say how large the bomb was or what it was made of.
"There appear to have been no personal injuries," a police source said.

The attack is the second on electricity generator Edelnor's offices in Lima in less than a month. On Feb. 9, suspected Maoist Shining Path rebels set off a bomb outside Edelnor's offices in the poor San Juan de Lurigancho east of Lima, police said.
No injuries were reported in that blast either. However, the building was slightly damaged and windows were blown out of nearby homes and stores.
Anti-terrorist police said they had no information on Tuesday night's blast yet but were investogating the incident.
The Shining Path is the larger of Peru's rebel groups. The smaller one, the Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA), holds 72 dignitaries hostage for a 99th day at the Japanese ambassador's home.
Wars unleashed by the two groups have killed 30,000 people and caused some $25 billion in infrastructure damage in Peru in the past 17 years.
